frontmatter_description: Diagnose whether in-group, out-group, stereotype, or belonging cues change how a person is interpreted or judged.
title: Group Identity
use_when: Use when the question asks how belonging to an in-group or out-group changes interpretation, judgment, or expectations.
Use when stereotypes, group labels, affiliation, or social identity shift how an act, remark, or person is evaluated.
Use when the key issue is whether group membership itself explains the observer's inference.
Use when the task is to identify identity-bound interpretation rather than role-based authority or interpersonal trust.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the main issue is power, status, authority, or role structure; use Power, Status, and Role instead.
Do not use when the main issue is trustworthiness based on past behavior; use Trust and Reputation instead.
Do not use when the issue is whether information may be shared or kept private; use Privacy, Secrets, and Boundaries instead.
Do not use when the issue is repair after offense, apology, or reconciliation; use Relationship Repair and Apology instead.
Do not use when the question is about literal belief, emotion, intention, or language meaning without any identity-bound inference.
decision_variable: whether group membership changes interpretation or evaluation
trigger_checklist: Is the answer driven by in-group versus out-group membership?
Are stereotypes, belonging, or identity labels affecting judgment?
Does the scene ask how the same behavior is read differently because of group identity?
Can the core explanation be stated as an identity-bound bias, expectation, or affiliation effect?
workflow: Identify the relevant group label or membership cue.
Ask whether the cue changes interpretation, expectation, or evaluation.
If yes, state the effect of belonging or stereotype on the judgment.
If the cue instead changes authority, trust, privacy, or repair, exit to the neighboring micro skill.

special_case.title: Identity cue without explicit stereotype
special_case.rule: If the scene never names a stereotype but still changes judgment because the person is treated as part of a group, this still belongs here.

worked_example.scene: A student from the debate team gives a short answer in class, and the teacher assumes the student is being strategic rather than unsure.
worked_example.question: Why is the answer interpreted that way?
worked_example.answer_logic: The teacher's interpretation is shaped by group identity and the stereotype attached to that group, so the effect of membership determines the judgment.

boundary_exit_rule: Exit to micro-46 if the main question is about hierarchy, authority, or formal role rather than group identity.
Exit to micro-45 if the main question is about whether someone is reliable based on history rather than belonging.
Exit to micro-48 if the question is about what information may be disclosed or concealed.
Exit to micro-49 if the question is about apology, harm repair, or restoring the relationship after offense.

references.route_signal: Use this micro unit when group membership, in-group/out-group status, stereotypes, or belonging changes how a person, act, or message is interpreted.
hard_boundary: Group-based evaluation, not trust from past conduct.
Belonging effect, not privacy or repair.
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not confuse 'they are the boss' with 'they are one of us.'
Do not infer trust or fault just because a group label is present.
Do not route scenes about hidden information or apology here unless identity-based judgment is central.
common_failure_modes: Treating role hierarchy as group identity.
Treating stereotype-based inference as simple attitude or emotion reading.
Overrouting any social scene with a group label, even when the real variable is trust, privacy, or repair.

minimal_pair.case: A manager gives the same criticism to two employees, and one is treated as being 'just strict' because of their role.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: This is about role and authority, not in-group or out-group identity.

minimal_pair.case: A new neighbor is judged as unfriendly because they belong to the rival local club.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The judgment is shaped by group membership and out-group bias.

boundary_stress_test: If the same behavior would be judged differently solely because of group membership, this matches.
If removing the group label removes the explanation, this matches.
If the scene still works the same after removing identity cues, do not use this unit.
references.generalization_note: This unit covers any identity-bound shift in interpretation or evaluation, including stereotypes, belonging, affiliation, and in-group/out-group bias, as long as the decisive variable is group membership rather than role, trust, privacy, or repair.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: A person is evaluated differently because they are seen as part of an in-group or out-group.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: A person is evaluated differently because they are the boss, expert, or subordinate.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: A person is judged for being unreliable, but the reason is their past broken promise rather than their group identity.

notes: Keep the unit narrow: it diagnoses identity-based interpretation, not general social judgment.
A stereotype can be explicit or implicit; the key is that group membership changes the inference.
If the question asks what someone feels about a group, do not use this unless the feeling itself is being shaped by belonging or stereotype.
core_question: Determine how in-group, out-group, stereotypes, or belonging shape interpretation and evaluation
